name: micro1
short: Robotics training data to order: first-person video of everyday and trade tasks, recorded by vetted paid contractors.

tasks: first-person (POV) and third-person video of domain experts performing real-world tasks
household task demonstrations recorded at home with a head-mounted smartphone (cooking, laundry, organising, packing, using basic tools)
skilled-trade demonstrations on real job sites (electrical, plumbing, carpentry, vehicle maintenance, valve and fixture replacement)
expert environment datasets: repair, assembly, industrial workflows, logistics, field operations
synchronised stereo video, IMU and multi-camera capture
robot interaction data captured in micro1's controlled robotics deployment lab
post-capture structuring: action-level annotation, temporal segmentation, hand/object interactions, 2D/3D annotation, tracking, QC and evaluation

pricing.notes: No buyer pricing is published; the robotics page has only a 'Get in touch' form. For scale only: contributors are paid per approved hour of recorded video (at-home recorder postings list $13-15/hour; a plumber posting lists $20-30/hour). That is labour cost, not a price.

latency.notes: No turnaround is stated. Contributors submit recordings on their own schedule and are paid biweekly for approved work; postings say start dates depend on shipping head-strap equipment.

freshness.typical_age: Recorded after a project is set up and contributors are onboarded
freshness.notes: MIT Technology Review reports micro1 says it holds tens of thousands of hours of footage; whether existing footage is also sold is not stated by micro1.

regions: real job sites and contributors' homes
coverage.notes: The everyday-tasks page says 'Open to everyone, globally'. MIT Technology Review (Apr 2026) reports thousands of contract workers in more than 50 countries, including India, Nigeria and Argentina. Some current at-home postings are limited to listed US states and US work eligibility. micro1 publishes no list of countries where it will collect for a buyer.

licensing.summary: No buyer-facing terms for robotics data are published; the Legal Center lists website, cookie, candidate and referral terms, and a 'Contractor Terms' heading with no document. The Data License Master Terms (undated on the page; binding only on an executed Order Form) govern data licensed TO micro1 by partner companies: they grant micro1 a perpetual, multi-tier sublicensable licence including AI training, and bar reselling that data as a standalone product. They do not cover data micro1 collects for a buyer. Contributor consent: per MIT Technology Review, workers know their footage trains robots but are not told which clients receive it.

human.method: Contributors pass an AI interview (Zara) and a device compatibility check, then a third-party identity check (scan of the physical ID plus a selfie matched to it; vendor not named) before a contract is issued.
human.unknown: How identity checks are done and whether each recording is tied to a verified person is not published; consent terms for recorded footage are not published.

application.unknown: Recording is limited to listed phones (iPhone 12 or later, Pixel 6-9, Galaxy S21 or later) on a head strap; a phone allowlist is not attestation, and no capture app or device attestation is documented. Capture in the provider's own app or rig is not a server-verified attestation (STANDARD §3).

camera.unknown: Not a signed capture, so none (STANDARD §3). What is stated: Head-mounted smartphone camera for POV video; synchronised stereo video, IMU and multi-camera pipelines for some projects. No C2PA or signed capture; micro1 is not on the C2PA conforming products list.

time.unknown: No signed or independently time-stamped capture times are documented.

location.unknown: No location proof is documented; recordings are made in contributors' homes or job sites.

content.method: Contributors follow written instructions (hands visible, natural speed); each video is reviewed by AI and a human and accepted or rejected; only approved recordings are paid; unsafe task performance is rejected.
content.unknown: Acceptance criteria and QC results are not published.

corroboration.unknown: No independent check of collected data is documented.

auth.how_to_get: Submit the 'Get in touch' form on micro1.ai/robotics describing the project; work is agreed with sales.

mcp.notes: No MCP server found; no micro1 entry in the official MCP Registry (searched 'micro1', 2026-10-26).

api.notes: No public buyer API for ordering or quoting data collection is documented.

delivery.basis: No turnaround is published. The robotics page offers only 'Get in touch'; contributor pages say recordings are made 'on your own schedule'.

payment.notes: No buyer payment terms or methods are published; there is no self-serve purchase.

requester.unknown: micro1 publishes no check of who commissions robotics data or for what. Its data-partnership pages say partner company data is licensed only to labs and enterprises in the US and allied countries; no such statement is made for robotics collection.

summary: micro1 collects robotics training data to order: first-person and third-person video of people doing household chores and skilled trade work, recorded on head-mounted phones by paid, AI-interviewed contractors, plus multi-camera and IMU capture and a robotics deployment lab. It also annotates and QCs the footage. Sales only: no prices, turnaround or buyer licence terms are published.

sources.claim: Expert-demonstrated POV and third-person capture; dataset structuring (labeling, tracking, 2D/3D annotation, QC); full-stack deployment lab; human demonstration pipelines; expert environment datasets (repair, assembly, industrial, logistics, field operations); synchronised stereo video, IMU, multi-camera; 'Get in touch' form
Household tasks recorded from point of view at home; 'Open to everyone, globally'; paid for approved recordings; AI interview, onboarding, instructions, biweekly pay
Trade tasks recorded on real job sites with wearable camera or phone (electrical, plumbing, carpentry, vehicle maintenance, valve and fixture replacement); plumbers $20-30/hour

At-home recorder posting: listed US states, US work eligibility, compatible phones (iPhone 12+, Pixel 6-9, Galaxy S21+), head strap, paid per hour of recorded video in line with guidelines, device check, AI interview, identity verification within 48 hours before contract; rate $13-15/hour
Data-Video Generalist (US) posting: same recording setup and requirements
